questions.question: For Athletics in 2025, what is the age eligibility range for boys' and girls' selection trials at SAI Chennai?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**12 to 18 years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The age eligibility range for boys' and girls' selection trials in **SAI Chennai** for Athletics in **2025** has been set as **12 to 18 years**.
 
• This age range ensures that young athletes falling within the developmental age group are provided opportunities to participate in national-level training and competitions.
 
• The selection trials aim to identify potential talent within the stipulated age group and nurture them under the **Sports Authority of India (SAI)** framework.
 
• The age range aligns with global norms for youth athletic competitions, ensuring participants are physically and mentally ready for rigorous training and competition.
 
• The trials are a part of SAI's commitment to improving sports standards in India by systematically identifying and training athletes from a young age.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sports Authority of India (SAI):**

 
 
• SAI is the apex national sports body established in **1984** under the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, Government of India.
 
• It is responsible for the development of sports infrastructure and nurturing talent across various sports disciplines.
 
• SAI operates through regional centers, including **SAI Chennai**, which focuses on sports development in southern India.
 
 
 
• **Age Eligibility in Sports:**
 
 
• Age eligibility criteria vary across sports and competitions to ensure fair play and proper categorization of athletes.
 
• In athletics, youth categories often range between **12 to 18 years**, allowing young athletes to hone their skills and transition into senior-level competitions.
 
• The age range also ensures proper physiological and psychological development of athletes, which is critical for long-term success in sports.
 
 
 
• **SAI Selection Trials:**
 
 
• Selection trials are conducted to identify talented athletes who can be trained under expert coaches and provided access to advanced facilities.
 
• Trials involve rigorous performance assessments, including fitness tests, skill demonstrations, and competition simulations.
 
• Selected athletes are enrolled in programs such as the **National Sports Academy** and are provided scholarships, accommodation, and other benefits.
 
 
 
• **Youth Development in Sports:**
 
 
• Youth development programs aim to nurture young athletes by providing them structured training, exposure to competitive events, and access to modern sports infrastructure.
 
• These programs are essential for creating a pipeline of talented athletes who can represent the country at international events like the Olympics and World Championships.
 
• India's focus on youth sports development has led to initiatives like **Khelo India** and **Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS)**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Selection Criteria:**

 
 
• Age eligibility is a critical factor in ensuring fairness and competitiveness in trials.
 
• Other criteria include physical fitness, skill level, and performance in previous competitions.
 
• Potential athletes are assessed by expert panels comprising coaches, physiotherapists, and sports scientists.
 
 
 
• **Khelo India Program:**
 
 
• Launched in **2018**, the Khelo India program aims to identify and nurture young talent in sports.
 
• It focuses on grassroots sports development and provides financial support to athletes.
 
• The program includes annual Khelo India Youth Games and scholarships for promising athletes.
 
 
 
• **Global Age Eligibility Standards:**
 
 
• Most international youth athletic competitions, such as the **World Youth Championships**, have similar age eligibility ranges.
 
• This ensures uniformity across nations and helps athletes transition smoothly into senior-level competitions.
 
• Countries like the **United States** and **Australia** follow similar youth development frameworks.

questions.question: In June 2025, which educational institution signed an MoU with VRDE to collaborate on advanced defence technologies?

__
 
• In **June 2025**, **COEP Technological University, Pune** signed a **Memorandum of Understanding (MoU)** with the **Vehicle Research and Development Establishment (VRDE)**, a laboratory under the Defence Research and Development Organisation (**DRDO**).
 
• This partnership aims to foster collaboration in the development of **advanced defence technologies** to strengthen India’s defence capabilities.
 
• The MoU focuses on **joint research**, **technology exchange**, and fostering innovation in areas such as **automotive engineering**, **armored vehicles**, and **mobility solutions**.
 
• COEP Technological University is renowned for its expertise in **engineering and applied sciences**, which aligns with VRDE’s focus on developing cutting-edge defence systems.
 
• Such collaborations are pivotal in enhancing the **indigenization** of defence technologies and reducing dependence on imports.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **COEP Technological University, Pune:**

 
 
• Established in **1854**, COEP is one of India’s oldest engineering institutions, located in **Pune, Maharashtra**.
 
• The university specializes in **mechanical engineering**, **robotics**, **AI-driven systems**, and **automotive research**.
 
• It has a history of contributing to innovation and research that supports national development goals.
 
• COEP collaborates with various industries and government organizations for **applied research** and **development projects**.
 
 
 
• **Vehicle Research and Development Establishment (VRDE):**
 
 
• VRDE is a key laboratory under **DRDO** located in **Ahmednagar, Maharashtra**.
 
• It specializes in the design, development, and testing of **military vehicles**, including tanks, armoured personnel carriers, and other mobility platforms.
 
• VRDE plays a critical role in **modernizing India’s defence forces** through indigenous technology development.
 
• Key achievements include contributions to the development of **Arjun Main Battle Tank** and other vehicles for the Indian Army.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Defence Research Collaborations:**
 
 
• Collaborations between academic institutions and defence organizations enhance **research capabilities** and foster **innovation**.
 
• These partnerships are crucial for reducing dependency on foreign technologies and achieving **self-reliance** in defence.
 
• Joint projects in areas like **armoured vehicle engineering**, **ballistic protection**, and **mobility systems** bolster national security.
 
• Such initiatives align with India’s **Atmanirbhar Bharat** mission for achieving self-sufficiency in technology and manufacturing.
 
 
 
• **Other Academic Institutions in the Context:**
 
 
• **National Institute of Technology, Warangal:** A premier engineering institution in **Telangana**, known for its work in structural engineering and material sciences but not related to VRDE collaborations.
 
• **Indian Institute of Science, Bengaluru:** Renowned for its contributions to aerospace and defence research, focusing on **advanced scientific methodologies**.
 
• **Rajasthan Technical University:** Primarily focused on technical education and research but does not have specific collaborations with VRDE in 2025.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• It facilitates the exchange of **knowledge**, **expertise**, and **resources** to develop indigenous systems for the Indian defence forces.
 
• This initiative underscores India’s commitment to strengthening its **defence sector** and achieving technological **self-reliance**.
 
 
 
• **Role of DRDO:**
 
 
• DRDO is India’s premier organization for defence research and development, working under the Ministry of Defence.

questions.question: Which Indian city was ranked the most polluted globally in the World Air Quality Report, 2024, released in March 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Delhi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Delhi** was ranked as the **most polluted city globally** according to the **World Air Quality Report, 2024**, released in **March 2025**.
 
• The report is published annually by **IQAir**, a Swiss air quality technology company, which provides global rankings based on **PM2.5 concentrations**.
 
• Delhi recorded extremely high levels of **PM2.5 pollution**, surpassing other cities globally. PM2.5 levels are a key metric for measuring air pollution as they represent fine particulate matter harmful to human health.
 
• The main contributors to Delhi's pollution include **vehicular emissions**, **industrial activities**, **construction dust**, **crop burning** in neighboring states, and **seasonal changes** like winter smog.
 
• Delhi's air quality has been a growing concern due to repeated instances of **air quality index (AQI)** readings reaching "severe" levels, particularly during winter months.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **World Air Quality Report:**

 
 
• The report by **IQAir** ranks cities and countries globally based on their average annual **PM2.5 concentration**, measured in micrograms per cubic meter.
 
• PM2.5 refers to particulate matter with a diameter of less than 2.5 micrometers, which can penetrate the lungs and bloodstream, causing severe health risks.
 
• Countries like **India, Pakistan, Bangladesh**, and **China** frequently top the rankings due to their industrial activities and urbanization.
 
• The report uses data from government monitoring stations and independent air quality monitoring systems.
 
 
 
• **Main Sources of Pollution in Delhi:**
 
 
• **Vehicular emissions:** Delhi has a high density of vehicles, contributing significantly to air pollution.
 
• **Crop residue burning:** Farmers in neighboring states like Punjab and Haryana burn crop residues, adding to Delhi's pollution during specific seasons.
 
• **Industrial emissions:** Industrial activities release harmful pollutants, including PM2.5 and PM10 particles.
 
• **Construction dust:** Ongoing infrastructure projects contribute to suspended particulate matter in the air.
 
• **Seasonal factors:** Winter weather conditions trap pollutants closer to the ground, worsening air quality.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Air Pollution:**
 
 
• Air pollution is linked to serious health issues, including **respiratory diseases**, **cardiovascular problems**, and **premature deaths**.
 
• Delhi frequently experiences public health emergencies due to toxic air quality, leading to school closures and advisories against outdoor activities.
 
• Long-term exposure to PM2.5 particles is associated with reduced life expectancy and increased risk of chronic illnesses.
 
 
 
• **Measures to Combat Pollution:**
 
 
• The Indian government has launched initiatives like the **National Clean Air Programme (NCAP)** to reduce PM2.5 levels by 20-30% by 2024.
 
• Delhi has implemented the **Odd-Even Scheme** to reduce vehicular emissions during peak pollution periods.
 
• Efforts to transition to cleaner fuels, such as compressed natural gas (CNG), and promote electric vehicles are underway.
 
• Strict regulations on construction activities and industrial emissions have been introduced to curb pollution.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **IQAir:** A Swiss-based air quality technology company that provides real-time air quality data and publishes annual reports on global pollution levels.
 
• **PM2.5 particles:** Fine particulate matter less than 2.5 micrometers in diameter, considered highly hazardous due to their ability to penetrate human lungs and bloodstream.
 
• **Air Quality Index (AQI):** A numerical scale used to measure and report air quality levels, ranging from "Good" to "Hazardous."
 
• **National Clean Air Programme (NCAP):** Launched by the Indian government in 2019, aiming to reduce air pollution in cities across India.
 
• **Seasonal Smog:** Smog formation during winters in Delhi is aggravated by temperature inversion and stagnant air conditions, trapping pollutants closer to the surface.

questions.question: In June 2025, Consumer Price Index (CPI) of India inflation for the financial year 2025-26 was projected at:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.037**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Consumer Price Index (CPI)** measures changes in the price level of a basket of consumer goods and services purchased by households over time. It is a key indicator of inflation.
 
• In **June 2025**, the **Consumer Price Index (CPI) inflation** for the financial year 2025-26 was projected at **3.7% (0.037 in decimal form)**. This projection indicates a moderate inflation level.
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** utilizes CPI as a primary measure to monitor and control inflation in the economy, ensuring price stability.
 
• Projection of CPI inflation is significant for formulating **monetary policies**, as inflation directly impacts economic growth, interest rates, and purchasing power.
 
• The projected value of 0.037 (3.7%) reflects efforts to maintain inflation within the RBI’s target range, which is typically **2%-6%** as per the **Monetary Policy Framework Agreement**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Consumer Price Index (CPI):**

 
 
• CPI is calculated by taking the weighted average of prices of a basket of goods and services essential for households, such as food, clothing, housing, and transportation.
 
• It is published monthly by the **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI)**.
 
• CPI is categorized into various groups: **CPI for Industrial Workers (CPI-IW), CPI for Agricultural Labourers (CPI-AL), CPI for Rural Labourers (CPI-RL), and CPI (Urban and Rural).**
 
• The base year for the current CPI in India is **2012**.
 
 
 
• **Inflation Targeting in India:**
 
 
• The **Monetary Policy Framework Agreement (2016)** between the Government of India and the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) sets an inflation target of **4% (+/- 2%)**.
 
• The RBI uses tools like the **repo rate**, reverse repo rate, and cash reserve ratio to control inflation.
 
• Maintaining inflation within the target ensures economic stability, growth, and protection of consumer purchasing power.
 
 
 
• **Importance of CPI Inflation Projections:**
 
 
• Projections guide **fiscal and monetary policies**, enabling the government and RBI to take proactive measures.
 
• They influence **interest rates**, investments, and savings, having a direct impact on the economy.
 
• Projections also help businesses and individuals make informed financial decisions.
 
 
 
• **Other Inflation Indices in India:**
 
 
• **Wholesale Price Index (WPI):** Measures price changes at the wholesale level and serves as a complementary indicator to CPI.
 
• **GDP Deflator:** Measures inflation in all domestically produced goods and services, offering a broader perspective compared to CPI and WPI.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Consumer Price Index (CPI)** is essential for understanding inflation trends and their impact on **economic stability and growth**.
 
• Inflation directly affects the purchasing power of individuals, making its control crucial for equitable economic development.
 
• Projections like 0.037 (3.7%) aid in maintaining inflation within a reasonable range, ensuring **macro-economic balance**.
 
• The RBI’s inflation-targeting strategy aligns with global best practices, prioritizing **price stability**.

questions.question: In June 2025, which two countries participated in Exercise SHAKTI, a biennial training engagement?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Exercise SHAKTI** is a biennial military exercise conducted between **India and France**. It focuses on enhancing defense cooperation and interoperability between the two nations.
 
• The exercise involves **joint training and operational exercises** between the **Indian Army** and the **French Army**, emphasizing counter-terrorism operations in semi-urban and urban environments.
 
• In June **2025**, the latest edition of Exercise SHAKTI was held, showcasing the **long-standing defense partnership** between **India** and **France**.
 
• The exercise aims to strengthen military-to-military relations and enhance mutual understanding of combat tactics, equipment, and strategies.
 
• Exercise SHAKTI is part of a broader framework of bilateral defense cooperation agreements, including naval and air force collaborations between India and France.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **India-France Defense Cooperation:**

 
 
• **India and France** share a robust defense partnership, including cooperation in defense equipment, technology transfer, and joint military exercises.
 
• The partnership extends to **naval, air force, and army collaborations**, including exercises such as **Exercise Varuna (naval)** and **Exercise Garuda (air force)**.
 
• France has been a key supplier of defense equipment to India, including the **Rafale fighter jets** and **Scorpene submarines**.
 
 
 
• **Counter-Terrorism Focus:**
 
 
• Exercise SHAKTI primarily emphasizes **counter-terrorism training**, enabling both nations to strengthen their capabilities to combat global terrorism.
 
• The training involves **scenario-based exercises**, including hostage rescue, urban warfare, and reconnaissance missions.
 
 
 
• **Global Strategic Partnership:**
 
 
• India and France have strengthened their strategic partnership through bilateral agreements covering defense, nuclear energy, and space cooperation.
 
• The Indo-French partnership plays a critical role in ensuring stability and security in the **Indo-Pacific region**.
 
 
 
• **Other Bilateral Exercises:**
 
 
• India conducts similar joint exercises with other nations, such as **Exercise Yudh Abhyas** (India-US), **Exercise Indra** (India-Russia), and **Exercise Sampriti** (India-Bangladesh).
 
• These exercises foster military cooperation, skill-sharing, and operational synergy among participating nations.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **India's Defense Strategy:**

 
 
• India has actively participated in joint military exercises to enhance its defense capabilities and strengthen international ties.
 
• These exercises are crucial for improving interoperability between forces and sharing expertise on modern warfare tactics.
 
 
 
• **France's Role in Global Defense:**
 
 
• France has been a prominent contributor to global defense and security, participating in joint exercises and peacekeeping missions worldwide.
 
• It emphasizes **counter-terrorism**, **cybersecurity**, and **maritime security** in its defense collaborations.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Exercise SHAKTI:**
 
 
• This exercise symbolizes the **long-standing friendship** and **shared values** of democracy, freedom, and mutual respect between India and France.
 
• It contributes to regional and global peace, ensuring preparedness against emerging security threats.

questions.question: In August 2025, NITI Aayog unveiled an innovative framework to evaluate and compare the advancement of States and Union Territories towards their Electric Mobility objectives named ________.

__
 
• **India Electric Mobility Index (IEMI)** was launched by **NITI Aayog** in **August 2025** as a framework to evaluate and compare the progress of **States and Union Territories** in achieving their electric mobility goals.
 
• The index aims to provide a **comprehensive assessment** of the efforts undertaken by various states and UTs to transition toward **sustainable transportation systems**.
 
• It covers **key parameters** such as policy implementation, infrastructure development, adoption rates of electric vehicles (EVs), and investment trends in electric mobility.
 
• The framework encourages **healthy competition** among states and UTs to accelerate their electric mobility initiatives, fostering innovation and collaboration in this sector.
 
• The **IEMI** is an essential component of India's broader push toward achieving **net-zero emissions** and promoting **clean energy usage** in the transportation sector.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• This name suggests a potential tool to measure the progress in EV adoption but is not the name of the framework launched by NITI Aayog.
 
• It could hypothetically focus on global or national trends in EV adoption and related technological advancements.
 
 
 
• **National E-Mobility Mission Plan Index:**
 
 
• The **National Electric Mobility Mission Plan (NEMMP)** was launched in **2013** by the Government of India to promote faster adoption and manufacturing of EVs.
 
• Though this plan plays an important role in India's electric mobility ecosystem, it is not the framework introduced in **2025**.
 
 
 
• **Sustainable Transport Index:**
 
 
• This name implies a broader focus on sustainable transportation, including public transport and other eco-friendly measures.
 
• However, it does not specifically focus on electric mobility as the **India Electric Mobility Index** does.
 
 
 
• **India Electric Mobility Index:**
 
 
• This framework is a **unique initiative** aimed at tracking and encouraging the progress of states and UTs toward electric mobility goals.
 
• By emphasizing data-driven decision-making, it aligns with India's commitment to achieving global **climate change mitigation** targets.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **EV Adoption in India:**

 
 
• India aims to achieve **30% EV penetration** in passenger vehicles, **70% in commercial vehicles**, and **80% in two- and three-wheelers** by **2030**.
 
• Government initiatives such as the **Faster Adoption and Manufacturing of Hybrid and Electric Vehicles (FAME)** scheme have been instrumental in driving EV adoption.
 
 
 
• **Infrastructure Challenges:**
 
 
• A lack of adequate **charging infrastructure** remains a major barrier to EV adoption in India.
 
• Efforts are underway to establish widespread charging networks, including **public-private partnerships**.
 
 
 
• **Global Context:**
 
 
• Countries like **Norway** and **China** are leading in EV adoption, serving as models for India's initiatives.
 
• India's ambitious goals align with global efforts to reduce **carbon emissions** and combat **climate change**.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of the 'Model Rules for Felling Trees in Agricultural Lands', released in 2025?

options.text: Easing business in agroforestry by streamlining rules

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Easing business in agroforestry by streamlining rules**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **'Model Rules for Felling Trees in Agricultural Lands'**, released in **2025**, aim to streamline the rules and regulations governing the felling of trees on agricultural lands. This is intended to remove unnecessary barriers and bureaucratic delays for farmers and businesses involved in agroforestry.
 
• The primary goal of these rules is to **encourage agroforestry**, which integrates trees into agricultural landscapes, enhancing both economic and ecological benefits. By simplifying the process, the rules aim to facilitate the widespread adoption of agroforestry practices.
 
• The initiative supports the government's broader objectives to **promote sustainable agriculture** and increase farmers' incomes by enabling them to derive economic benefits from tree farming and timber production.
 
• Under these rules, the process for obtaining permissions to cut trees on agricultural land has been made faster and more transparent. Farmers can now focus on planting and harvesting trees without excessive regulatory burden.
 
• The **environmental safeguards** in the model rules ensure that tree felling is balanced with reforestation efforts, promoting ecological sustainability while supporting economic growth in rural areas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Agroforestry Benefits:**

 
 
• **Economic Benefits:** Farmers can earn additional income by growing and selling timber, fruits, or other tree-based products.
 
• **Environmental Benefits:** Agroforestry helps in soil conservation, water retention, and carbon sequestration, reducing greenhouse gas emissions.
 
• **Biodiversity:** It promotes biodiversity by creating habitats for various flora and fauna.
 
• **Climate Resilience:** Trees act as windbreaks and provide shade, helping to stabilize microclimates and protect crops from extreme weather.
 
 
 
• **Previous Agroforestry Initiatives:**
 
 
• **National Agroforestry Policy (2014):** India became the first country to introduce a dedicated agroforestry policy to promote the integration of trees into agricultural landscapes.
 
• **Sub-Mission on Agroforestry:** Launched in 2016-17 under the National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture, this initiative provides financial and technical support to farmers adopting agroforestry practices.
 
 
 
• **Streamlined Process for Tree Felling:**
 
 
• The 2025 model rules are designed to reduce delays in granting tree-felling permits, which previously discouraged farmers from planting trees on their land.
 
• The rules also emphasize the use of digital platforms for applications and approvals, ensuring greater transparency and efficiency.
 
 
 
• **Agroforestry and the Economy:**
 
 
• The agroforestry sector contributes significantly to India's economy by providing raw materials for industries like paper, furniture, and bioenergy.
 
• Encouraging agroforestry can help India meet its climate goals, such as increasing forest cover and achieving carbon neutrality targets.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Challenges in Agroforestry:**

 
 
• Farmers often face challenges such as lack of awareness, high initial costs, and complicated legal requirements for tree felling.
 
• The 2025 model rules address these issues by simplifying regulations and providing support for capacity-building initiatives.
 
 
 
• **Global Context:**
 
 
• Countries like **China** and **Brazil** have successfully integrated agroforestry into their agricultural policies, reaping significant economic and environmental benefits.
 
• India's initiatives are in line with global efforts to promote sustainable agriculture and combat deforestation.
 
 
 
• **Key Data:** Agroforestry contributes to **1.5-2% of India's GDP** and is a critical component of the country's strategy to achieve **33% forest cover** under its National Forest Policy.
 
• Farmers adopting agroforestry under government schemes have seen an **average income increase of 20-30%** over traditional farming methods.

questions.question: When did Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) and the Indian Navy conduct the successful flight-test of indigenously-developed Vertically-Launched Short-Range Surface-to-Air Missile (VLSRSAM) from the Integrated Test Range (ITR), Chandipur off the coast of Odisha?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Wed Mar 26 2025 00:00:00 GMT+0530 (India Standard Time)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)** and the **Indian Navy** conducted a successful flight-test of the **Vertically-Launched Short-Range Surface-to-Air Missile (VLSRSAM)** on **March 26, 2025**.
 
• The test was conducted at the **Integrated Test Range (ITR), Chandipur**, located off the coast of **Odisha**, India.
 
• The **VLSRSAM** is an **indigenously-developed missile**, showcasing India's focus on enhancing its **self-reliance** in defense technology.
 
• The missile was designed to provide **short-range air defense** capabilities, targeting aerial threats such as fighter aircraft, helicopters, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), and other airborne objects.
 
• The flight-test was aimed at evaluating the missile's **performance parameters**, including its precision, launch mechanism, and effectiveness in intercepting aerial targets.
 
• This marks a significant milestone for India's defense sector, reinforcing its **Make in India** initiative in weaponry development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO):**

 
 
• DRDO is India's premier organization for **research and development in defense technologies**.
 
• Established in **1958**, DRDO operates under the **Ministry of Defence**.
 
• Its mission is to develop state-of-the-art systems and technologies for India's armed forces, including **missiles, radar systems, combat vehicles, and electronics**.
 
• Some notable achievements include the development of **Agni and Prithvi series of missiles**, **Tejas fighter aircraft**, and **Astra air-to-air missile**.
 
 
 
• **Indian Navy's Role:**
 
 
• The Indian Navy plays a pivotal role in safeguarding India's maritime interests and ensuring **security in the Indian Ocean region**.
 
• Collaborating with DRDO, the Navy supports the development and testing of advanced weapons and systems for enhancing naval capabilities.
 
• Its partnership in the VLSRSAM development highlights the importance of integrating indigenous technologies into naval defense systems.
 
 
 
• **Integrated Test Range (ITR), Chandipur:**
 
 
• Located in **Odisha**, ITR Chandipur serves as a hub for testing missiles and other defense systems developed by DRDO.
 
• It is equipped with advanced facilities for assessing missile trajectories, flight dynamics, and target engagement capabilities.
 
• The site has been used for testing various weapons, including **Ballistic Missile Defense (BMD) systems** and **surface-to-air missiles**.
 
 
 
• **Vertically-Launched Short-Range Surface-to-Air Missile (VLSRSAM):**
 
 
• The VLSRSAM is part of India's initiative to develop **indigenous missile systems** for strengthening its defense capabilities.
 
• It is designed to intercept and neutralize **short-range aerial threats**, ensuring the protection of critical assets and installations.
 
• The missile's vertical launch capability enables its deployment on **naval ships**, providing flexibility and operational efficiency.
 
• Its development aligns with India's goal of achieving **self-reliance** in defense technology under the **Make in India** initiative.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of Indigenous Missile Development:**

 
 
• Indigenous development reduces **dependence on foreign suppliers** and boosts the domestic defense industry.
 
• It enhances India's **strategic autonomy** and provides a competitive edge in global defense markets.
 
• Such initiatives contribute to **job creation** and the development of high-tech infrastructure within the country.
 
 
 
• **Make in India Initiative:**
 
 
• Launched by the Government of India in **2014**, this initiative aims to transform India into a **global manufacturing hub**.
 
• It emphasizes fostering innovation, enhancing skill development, and attracting investments in key sectors, including **defense**.
 
• The development of systems like VLSRSAM showcases the successful implementation of this initiative in the defense domain.
 
 
 
• **Global Context:**
 
 
• India's advancements in missile technology place it among countries like the **USA, Russia, and China**, which have robust indigenous defense capabilities.
 
• Such developments contribute to India's stature as a **regional and global security provider** in the Indian Ocean region.

questions.question: In September 2025, the Ministry of Environment, Forest, and Climate Change introduced which of the following to enhance environmental compliance and governance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Environment Audit Rules, 2025**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Environment Audit Rules, 2025** were introduced by the **Ministry of Environment, Forest, and Climate Change** in September 2025 to enhance **environmental compliance and governance**.
 
• These rules aim to establish a structured mechanism for conducting **environmental audits** across industries, ensuring adherence to environmental laws and regulations.
 
• The audits focus on evaluating the implementation of **sustainability practices**, compliance with environmental norms, and the impact of industrial activities on ecosystems.
 
• The rules emphasize the adoption of **transparent reporting mechanisms**, where industries must submit environmental audit reports periodically to regulatory authorities.
 
• The initiative is designed to strengthen the capacity of industries to address **climate change challenges**, reduce pollution, and promote sustainable development. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Environmental Audits:**

 
 
• Environmental audits are **systematic evaluations** of an organization's environmental compliance, focusing on adherence to **laws, regulations, and standards**.
 
• The audits help identify areas of improvement, ensuring industries take corrective actions to mitigate their environmental impact.
 
• They involve assessing **waste management**, energy usage, water conservation, air quality monitoring, and biodiversity protection. 
 
• Global examples include initiatives like the **ISO 14001 environmental management system**, which sets standards for environmental audits.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Environment, Forest, and Climate Change:**
 
 
• This ministry is the nodal agency responsible for implementing policies and programs related to **environment protection**, **forest conservation**, and combating **climate change** in India.
 
• It formulates rules, regulations, and guidelines under various acts like the **Environment Protection Act, 1986**, and the **Air and Water Acts**.
 
• Some of its notable initiatives include the **National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC)** and the **Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning Authority (CAMPA).**
 
 
 
• **Comparison of Options:**
 
 
• **Sustainable Practices and Audit Guidelines, 2025:** This option emphasizes sustainable practices but does not specifically address environmental audits. It is not the correct answer.
 
• **Environmental Sustainability and Compliance Rules, 2025:** While it highlights compliance, it lacks the direct emphasis on audits, making it incorrect.
 
• **Green Business Certification Framework, 2025:** This framework focuses on certifying businesses for sustainable practices but does not encompass a structured audit process as outlined by the Environment Audit Rules, 2025.
 
 
 
• **Important Points:**
 
 
• **Environmental compliance:** It refers to industries adhering to environmental laws, regulations, and standards to minimize their ecological impact.
 
• **Periodic reporting:** The Environment Audit Rules, 2025 mandate industries to submit environmental audit reports to track compliance and identify gaps.
 
• **Climate change mitigation:** The audits play a vital role in helping industries implement strategies to reduce carbon emissions and enhance sustainability.
 
• Such initiatives align with India's commitments under the **Paris Agreement** and its **Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs)**.

questions.question: Who was appointed as the RBI Deputy Governor in April 2025, becoming one of the key figures in shaping India’s financial and monetary policy?

__
 
• **Poonam Gupta** was appointed as the **RBI Deputy Governor** in **April 2025**, a significant role in shaping India's **financial and monetary policy**.
 
• She is known for her expertise in **macroeconomic research**, and her appointment reflects the government's focus on strengthening the **economic policy framework**.
 
• Poonam Gupta previously served as the **Director-General of the National Council of Applied Economic Research (NCAER)**, India's premier economic research institute, which focuses on high-quality, evidence-based economic research.
 
• Her contributions have been pivotal in areas such as **economic growth**, **trade policy**, and **public finance**, making her a prominent figure in India's economic policymaking space.
 
• As Deputy Governor, Poonam Gupta will play a key role in managing aspects such as **monetary policy formulation**, **foreign exchange management**, and **financial market development**.

__
 
• **Reserve Bank of India (RBI):**

 
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India** is India's central bank and regulatory authority responsible for the **issuance of currency** and **management of monetary policy**.
 
• It was established on **April 1, 1935**, under the **Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934**.
 
• The RBI is responsible for **regulating the banking system**, ensuring financial stability, and overseeing India's **foreign exchange reserves**.
 
• The **Deputy Governors** of RBI assist the Governor in executing the bank's functions and are usually assigned specific portfolios like **monetary policy**, **banking regulation**, or **financial market development**.
 
 
 
• **Key Functions of RBI:**
 
 
• **Monetary Policy:** Formulating policies to control inflation, stabilize the currency, and promote growth.
 
• **Currency Issuance:** Responsible for issuing and managing the supply of the Indian currency.
 
• **Financial Regulation:** Regulating and supervising banks and other financial institutions.
 
• **Foreign Exchange Management:** Managing India's foreign exchange reserves and ensuring stability in the foreign exchange market.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Deputy Governors:**
 
 
• The Deputy Governors are appointed to oversee specific aspects of the RBI's functions, ensuring effective policymaking and implementation.
 
• They play a crucial role in representing the RBI in interactions with **global financial institutions** and **government bodies**.
 
• Deputy Governors are often involved in drafting policies related to **economic growth**, **financial inclusion**, and **banking reforms**.
 
 
 
• **Other Notable RBI Deputy Governors:**
 
 
• **Shaktikanta Das:** Served as RBI Governor after holding senior positions in the Ministry of Finance.
 
• **Arundhati Bhattacharya:** Former Chairperson of the State Bank of India, known for her contributions to India's banking sector.
 
• **Nirmala Sitharaman:** India's current Finance Minister, although she has not served as Deputy Governor, her policy decisions significantly influence the RBI.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Selection Process:**

 
 
• The appointment of RBI Deputy Governors is typically done by the **Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC)**, headed by the Prime Minister.
 
• Candidates are selected based on their **expertise in economics, banking, or finance**.
 
 
 
• **Challenges for the Deputy Governor:**
 
 
• Managing inflation and ensuring economic stability amidst global uncertainties.
 
• Strengthening India's financial system and increasing **financial inclusion**.
 
• Formulating policies to address challenges in areas like **non-performing assets (NPAs)** and **digital banking**.
